A walkthrough of what the app can do and how to reach it — by touch, by screen reader, or by switch. Everything here works fully offline.
Playback controls announce the action they perform — Play, Pause, Next, Previous, Shuffle, Repeat, Favourite.
Titles on this screen are marked as headings, so you can jump between sections instead of swiping through every item.
FastBeat follows your system text size. Change it in Android Settings, under Display then Font size.
Light and dark modes and the accent colour are in the Me tab. Pick whichever is easiest for you to read.
Every video swipe gesture has a button equivalent except brightness. Tap once to show the controls, then use the on-screen buttons. Volume also responds to your device\'s volume keys.

Browse videos grouped by the folder they live in. Tap one to play it full screen, with on-screen controls for play, skip, and jumping ten seconds either way. Bookmarks, subtitle and audio track selection, playback speed, screen rotation, aspect ratio, and Picture-in-Picture are all in the top control bar.
Your library organised by tracks, albums, artists, decades, and playlists. Tap a track to start playing. The mini-player stays at the bottom so you can keep browsing while it plays.
Every image on your device in a scrolling grid. Tap one to open it full screen and swipe between images from there.
Your listening time, daily streak, most played tracks, and recent history. Themes, light and dark mode, and this guide live here too.
Open the full player by tapping the mini-player. Alongside play, skip, and seek you will find:
Toggle either from the main control row. The current state is announced when focused.
Mark the current track so it shows up in your Me tab.
In the overflow menu. The current speed is shown next to the option.
Presets, bass boost, and virtualizer, in the overflow menu. Some devices do not support audio effects — the sheet will say so.
Appears in the overflow menu between 10 PM and 5 AM, or any time a timer is already running. Playback pauses when it ends.
Save the current track into any playlist from the overflow menu.
Open the queue from the Now Playing screen to see what is coming up.
Drag a track by its handle to move it. Reordering is unavailable while shuffle is on — turn shuffle off first.
Take a single track out of the queue without stopping playback.
Turn the queue you are listening to into a permanent playlist.
From any track\'s menu, queue it immediately after the current one instead of at the end.
Your queue and position are saved, so closing the app and reopening it picks up where you left off.
These work anywhere on the video surface. Each one shows an on-screen indicator as you drag.
Swipe up or down on the left
Swipe up or down on the right
Ignore all gestures so a stray touch cannot interrupt playback

While something is playing, a compact bar sits at the bottom of the screen with previous and next controls. Tap it to open the full player. It stays put as you move between tabs, so you never lose what is playing.
Filter tracks, albums, and playlists as you type.
Change the order of any list; your choice is remembered for next time.
Drag down on any media list to rescan your device for new files.
Available from a file\'s menu. On Android 11 and newer the system asks you to confirm; if only some files in a selection can be changed, FastBeat tells you which.
Built automatically from how you listen, in the Music tab: Most Played, Recently Added, Forgotten, Never Played, and Most Skipped. They update themselves — there is nothing to maintain.
Your data stays on your device

FastBeat has no network access. Your library, listening history, streaks, and playlists never leave your phone — which also means there is no cloud backup, so keep your own copies of anything irreplaceable.
